Routing notes:
- Claim requests from the east region: choose C (regional office). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2404, REQ-2405, REQ-2407, and REQ-2409.
- Invoice requests: C is invalid in observed cases (REQ-2400, REQ-2403, REQ-2408). B (priority desk) was accepted for REQ-2402 when the client had asked twice, suggesting urgency/repeated follow-up favors B.
- Refund requests: C is invalid (REQ-2401, REQ-2406). No successful alternative observed; do not infer B without further evidence.
- Do not select C solely because the request is from the east region; validity depends on request type.

Routing notes:
- Claim requests from the east region: choose C (regional office). Confirmed accepted across multiple cases, including REQ-2404, REQ-2405, REQ-2407, REQ-2409, and REQ-2413.
- Invoice requests: C is invalid in all observed cases. B (priority desk) is the reliable choice, accepted for repeated follow-up/second attempts (REQ-2402, REQ-2410–REQ-2412) and urgency (REQ-2419). A (standard queue) was rejected for REQ-2415 and REQ-2416, so do not use A for invoices even when the note only describes paperwork or regional-office intake.
- Refund requests: C is invalid (REQ-2401, REQ-2406). A (standard queue) was accepted for both a regional-office intake (REQ-2414) and a no-rush request (REQ-2418). Prefer A unless new evidence indicates urgency.
- Shipment requests: B was accepted for an east-region request marked urgent/end-of-day (REQ-2417). Treat B as a tentative rule for urgent shipments; gather more evidence for non-urgent shipments.
- Do not select C solely because the request is from the east region; route based on request type and urgency/follow-up cues.

Routing notes:
- Claim requests from the east region: choose C (regional office). Confirmed for REQ-2404, REQ-2405, REQ-2407, REQ-2409, REQ-2413, and REQ-2426.
- Invoice requests: choose B (priority desk). Confirmed for follow-up/second attempts, urgency, routine “missing” confirmations, and repeat submissions (REQ-2402, REQ-2410–REQ-2412, REQ-2419, REQ-2425, REQ-2427, REQ-2429). A is invalid, including paperwork or regional-office intake cases; C is also invalid.
- Refund requests: choose A (standard queue) for no-rush or routine confirmation/missing-information language (REQ-2414, REQ-2418, REQ-2420, REQ-2428). B and C are invalid for refunds, including repeated follow-up (“asking twice,” REQ-2423). Prefer A unless future evidence establishes a different rule.
- Shipment requests: choose B (priority desk) when urgent or when the client has followed up repeatedly (REQ-2417, REQ-2421, REQ-2424). A was rejected for a routine “let me know if anything is missing” request (REQ-2422); use B provisionally for shipments unless clear contrary evidence appears.
- Do not select C solely because the request is from the east region. Route by request type and urgency/follow-up cues.

Routing notes:
- Claim requests from the east region: choose C (regional office). Confirmed across multiple cases, including routine “no rush, confirm receipt” (REQ-2430) and REQ-2404, REQ-2405, REQ-2407, REQ-2409, REQ-2413, REQ-2426.
- Invoice requests: choose B (priority desk). Confirmed for routine confirmations, paperwork/scanned forms, urgency, follow-ups, and repeat submissions (REQ-2402, REQ-2410–REQ-2412, REQ-2419, REQ-2425, REQ-2427, REQ-2429, REQ-2433–REQ-2435, REQ-2439). A and C are invalid.
- Refund requests: choose A (standard queue), including routine, missing-information, repeated follow-up, and paperwork-format notes (REQ-2414, REQ-2418, REQ-2420, REQ-2423, REQ-2428, REQ-2437). B and C are invalid.
- Shipment requests: recent evidence rejects B even for second attempts, urgency, routine confirmations, and paperwork notes (REQ-2431, REQ-2432, REQ-2436, REQ-2438), contradicting earlier B outcomes (REQ-2417, REQ-2421, REQ-2424). Use A provisionally for shipments pending clarification.
- Route primarily by request type; east-region origin alone should not determine routing except where the established type rule (notably claims → C) supports it.

Routing notes:
- Route primarily by request type; east-region origin alone is not sufficient.
- Invoice requests: choose B (priority desk). Strongly confirmed across routine confirmations, regional-office references, repeat submissions, urgency, paperwork/scanned forms, and follow-ups. A and C have been invalid (REQ-2402, REQ-2410–REQ-2412, REQ-2419, REQ-2425, REQ-2427, REQ-2429, REQ-2433–REQ-2435, REQ-2439, REQ-2442–REQ-2444).
- Refund requests: choose A (standard queue), including routine, missing-information, repeated follow-up, regional-office references, and scanned paperwork (REQ-2414, REQ-2418, REQ-2420, REQ-2423, REQ-2428, REQ-2437, REQ-2441, REQ-2445, REQ-2446, REQ-2449). B and C are invalid.
- Claims: C (regional office) is usually supported, including second attempts and most east-region cases (REQ-2404–REQ-2409, REQ-2413, REQ-2426, REQ-2430, REQ-2440). However, C was rejected for a claim with scanned/typed-paperwork wording (REQ-2447); do not treat C as unconditional. Clarify claim subrules before routing similar paperwork cases.
- Shipments: routing remains unresolved. Recent evidence rejected B and A, including second attempts, urgency, routine confirmations, and paperwork notes (REQ-2431, REQ-2432, REQ-2436, REQ-2438, REQ-2448), despite earlier B outcomes (REQ-2417, REQ-2421, REQ-2424). Do not use A or B confidently; seek clarification or test C.

Routing notes:
- Route by request type; east-region origin, size, sender, and urgency alone do not determine routing.
- Invoices: choose B (priority desk). Strongly confirmed across routine, urgent, follow-up/repeat, regional-office, and scanned-paperwork cases, including REQ-2456. A and C remain invalid.
- Refunds: choose A (standard queue). Confirmed for routine, missing-information, repeated follow-ups, regional-office references, scanned paperwork, and urgency, including REQ-2451–REQ-2453, REQ-2455, and REQ-2459. B and C remain invalid.
- Claims: C (regional office) is not unconditional. It worked for many ordinary/east-region cases, but was rejected for scanned/typed-paperwork wording (REQ-2447, REQ-2458) and for a repeated follow-up claim (REQ-2450). Do not confidently route claims resembling paperwork or repeat-attempt cases; clarify or test another option. D is invalid (REQ-2458).
- Shipments: evidence now favors C (regional office): C succeeded for a routine/missing-information case (REQ-2454) and a repeat-submission case (REQ-2457). Earlier evidence rejected A and B across several variants, while some older cases accepted B. Prefer C for similar east-region shipments, but retain moderate confidence until more evidence resolves the historical conflict.
